title: 1. Introduction to rLifting
text: Offline mode access full signal. threshold_method = "universal" (default), estimates single noise variance σ̂\hat{\sigma} finest-level details d1d_1 via MAD propagates threshold across levels via α/β\alpha/\beta recursion (Liu, Mi, & Mao, 2014); robust white Gaussian noise. threshold_method = "sure", decomposition level gets MAD-based σ̂j\hat{\sigma}_j SURE-optimal λj\lambda_j, flexible wavelet biorthogonal noise heterogeneous across scales. paths run single C++ pass (LWT → threshold → ILWT) R allocations. Key parameters: shrinkage: "semisoft" recommended default. reduces bias compared soft thresholding avoids ringing hard thresholding. Also available: "hard", "soft", "scad" (Antoniadis & Fan, 2001); see Section 4 extensions vignette visual comparison. threshold_method: "universal" (default; VisuShrink finest-level threshold Donoho & Johnstone, 1994, propagated coarser levels via α/β recursion Liu, Mi, & Mao, 2014, ) "sure" (SureShrink: per-level SURE-minimising threshold, case alpha beta inert). Use tune_alpha_beta() pick α β automatically minimising SURE. alpha: controls threshold decays fine coarse levels via recursion λk=λk−1⋅(k−1)/(k+α−1)\lambda_k = \lambda_{k-1} \cdot (k-1)/(k+\alpha-1) (Liu, Mi, & Mao, 2014). Smaller values (e.g. 0.1) keep threshold nearly flat across levels; larger values (e.g. 5) decay aggressively, suppressing coarse-level coefficients. α=0\alpha = 0 threshold constant across levels. beta: scales universal threshold λ1=β⋅σ̂⋅2log⁡n\lambda_1 = \beta \cdot \hat{\sigma} \cdot \sqrt{2 \log n} (Donoho & Johnstone, 1994). Values 1.0 increase smoothing; 1.0 reduce . extension: five boundary modes available: "symmetric" (default), "periodic", "zero", "local_linear" (linear extrapolation; neighbourhood size controlled ll_k, default 4), "one_sided" (asymmetric renormalised filter edge; useful causal mode). See vignette("v04-boundary-modes") full discussion.

title: 1. Introduction to rLifting
text: Causal mode processes signal samples arrived sequentially: output sample tt depends recent window_size samples xt−W+1,…,xtx_{t - W + 1}, \dots, x_t (never future samples). ring buffer evicts older history new samples arrive, memory bounded WW regardless total signal length. first window_size − 1 output samples returned -(buffer warm-phase); window_size-th sample first filtered output. warm-, output fully causal filtered. window_size main tuning parameter: larger windows give better frequency resolution stable threshold estimates, increase latency memory. value 128–512 typical. update_freq controls often adaptive threshold recomputed. update_freq = 1 recomputes every sample (maximum adaptivity, slightly CPU). stationary noise, update_freq = 10–50 reduces overhead without meaningful accuracy loss.
code: window_size = 255 # must be odd; forced odd automatically if even is supplied causal_levels = levels # same depth as offline for a fair comparison (Section 8)  causal_clean = denoise_signal_causal(   doppler_example$noisy,   scheme,   window_size = window_size,   levels = causal_levels,   shrinkage = "semisoft",   update_freq = 1  # recompute threshold every sample (maximum adaptivity) )

Native irregular-grid support: pass sorted t vector pipeline function predict step uses Lagrange interpolation actual sample positions — separate regularisation step. regular grids, rLifting ~40× faster per sample wavethresh ~40,000× faster adlift/nlt, trailing wavethresh ~18% geometric mean MSE level. irregular grids, ~20,000× faster adlift comparable accuracy (within ~10% six seven signals). title: High-Performance Wavelet Lifting Transforms
text: Three processing modes API: denoise_signal_offline, denoise_signal_causal, new_wavelet_stream. Six built-wavelets: haar, db2, cdf53, cdf97, dd4, lazy. Extensible via lift_step() + custom_wavelet(). Four shrinkage methods: hard, soft, semisoft (default), SCAD (Antoniadis & Fan, 2001). Two threshold-selection rules: universal (VisuShrink, recursive α/β decay) SURE (SureShrink, per-level Stein risk). tune_alpha_beta() minimises SURE select α β automatically. Five boundary extensions: symmetric (default), periodic, zero, local_linear (OLS extrapolation, neighbourhood ll_k), one_sided (renormalised filter edge). Irregular-grid support every mode: pass t batch functions, t_val per sample stream closure. Diagnostic suite: diagnose_wavelet() verifies perfect reconstruction, vanishing moments, orthogonality, compact support, shift sensitivity.

title: rLifting 1.0.0
text: Native irregular-grid support: pass sorted t vector denoise_signal_offline(), denoise_signal_causal(), t_val per sample stream closure new_wavelet_stream(). predict step uses Lagrange interpolation conditioned actual sample positions — separate regularisation required. Two new boundary extensions: local_linear (OLS extrapolation configurable neighbourhood ll_k) one_sided (renormalised filter edge), bringing total five alongside existing symmetric, periodic, zero. SureShrink threshold rule (threshold_method = "sure"): per-level Stein Unbiased Risk Estimator, complementing existing universal (VisuShrink) rule. SCAD shrinkage (shrinkage = "scad"): Smoothly Clipped Absolute Deviation (Antoniadis & Fan, 2001), added alongside existing hard, soft, semisoft shrinkages. tune_alpha_beta(): automatic selection recursive threshold parameters α β minimising SURE signal. diagnose_wavelet(): verification suite custom wavelets — perfect reconstruction, vanishing moments, orthogonality, compact support, shift sensitivity. Seven benchmark datasets bundled: benchmark_rlifting, benchmark_wavethresh, benchmark_adlift, benchmark_nlt, benchmark_rlifting_irregular, benchmark_adlift_irregular, benchmark_nlt_irregular — based 1,000 Monte Carlo replications per configuration. Eight vignettes: introduction, thresholding tuning, causal/stream, boundary modes, irregular grids, extensions, full cross-package benchmarks, real-world case study (BabyECG infant cardiac monitoring).

text: CRAN release: 2026-02-20 Initial release package. Implements high-performance Wavelet Lifting Transforms. Unified offline (batch) denoising via denoise_signal_offline(). Causal (sliding-window) filtering via denoise_signal_causal(). Sample--sample stream processing via new_wavelet_stream(). Adaptive recursive thresholding (universal rule, hard/soft/semisoft shrinkage). Zero-allocation ‘C++’ core via ‘Rcpp’. Six built-wavelets: Haar, DB2, CDF 5/3, CDF 9/7, DD4, Lazy.
